title: SPECULATIVE ILLUSIONS

lists.name: SPECULATIVE ILLUSIONS
items: State-specificity of society (as opposed to a fundamental indeterminacy, or intrinsic and irreducible ambiguity, of its would-be 'states')
Uniqueness of physical reality (continuity of the world, uniqueness of causal regularity)
Absolute size (or unique spatial order and hierarchy)
Time (or unique temporal order and hierarchy)
That some things are truly impossible
Simplicity of universe (or finite complexity of anything)
Absolute necessity (that some things are really necessary)
Absolute independence of events (of any physical events in the cosmos)
Absolute oblivion (that we ever truly forget anything)
Openness or Infinitude of universe (of space, time, etc)

notes: total items: 90. NOTE: 'Speculative' means that the illusion referred to may or may not be real—or the thing referred to may or may not be illusory. Either the evidence that present-day experimental data, theory, and logic provide is too poor to decide whether the illusion is real, or it makes the reality of the would-be illusion seem less than probable. Yet all of the hypothetical illusions that are included in the list below are reasonable, and good arguments can be made in support of their reality.
